item.text: {"case_id":"SHC026","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C13","C03","C11"],"selected_candidate_label":"C13","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C13 is a highly plausible direct drafting template for the child letter. Both are congressional notifications of additional UNITA sanctions, and they share a distinctive paragraph-by-paragraph sequence: report the exercise of statutory authority; state that the 1993 emergency circumstances remain unresolved; recount successive Security Council sanctions and Lusaka Protocol noncompliance; summarize a newly issued Executive order in numbered form; discuss humanitarian exemptions; define UNITA through the same three components; explain how the measures constrain UNITA and advance the peace process; and promise support for lifting sanctions upon UNITA's transition to an unarmed political party. Much of this language is nearly verbatim, while the operative sanctions and cited resolutions are updated. C03 supplies closely related UNITA sanctions machinery reflected in the child, and C11 supplies the original UNITA framework, but neither matches the later letter's form and full rhetorical structure as closely as C13.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I hereby report to the Congress that I have exercised my statutory authority to take additional steps with respect to the actions and policies of the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA) and the national emergency declared in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE].","parent_excerpt":"I hereby report to the Congress that I have exercised my statutory authority to take additional steps with respect to the actions and policies of the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA) and the national emergency declared in [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE].","explanation":"The opening notification sentence is identical."},{"child_excerpt":"The circumstances that led to the declaration on September 26, 1993, of a national emergency have not been resolved. The actions and policies of UNITA continue to pose an unusual and extraordinary threat to the foreign policy of the United States.","parent_excerpt":"The circumstances that led to the declaration on September 26, 1993, of a national emergency have not been resolved. The actions and policies of UNITA pose a continuing unusual and extraordinary threat to the foreign policy of the United States.","explanation":"Distinctive emergency-justification language is reused with only a minor word-order change."},{"child_excerpt":"The order defines UNITA to include: (1) the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola; (2) the Armed Forces for the Liberation of Angola (FALA); and (3) any person acting or purporting to act for or on behalf of the foregoing, including the Center for Democracy in Angola (CEDA).","parent_excerpt":"Under the terms of this order, UNITA includes: (1) the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola; (2) the Armed Forces for the Liberation of Angola (FALA); and (3) any person acting or purporting to act for or on behalf of the foregoing, including the Center for Democracy in Angola (CEDA).","explanation":"The same three-part definition appears in the same position in the letter structure."},{"child_excerpt":"It is particularly important for the United States and the international community to demonstrate to UNITA the necessity of completing the peace process in Angola.","parent_excerpt":"It is particularly important for the United States and the international community to demonstrate to UNITA the necessity of completing the peace process in Angola.","explanation":"The policy explanation is copied verbatim."},{"child_excerpt":"When UNITA fully complies with its obligations and completes its transition from an armed movement to an unarmed political party, the United States will support measures lifting these sanctions.","parent_excerpt":"When UNITA fully complies with its obligations and completes its transition from armed movement to unarmed political party, the United States will support measures lifting these sanctions.","explanation":"The concluding condition for lifting sanctions is substantively identical and nearly verbatim."}]}
